title: First Fitting singular subscheme of a morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes that is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ be the sheaf of relative Kähler differentials [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Let $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subset X$ be an affine open mapping into an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(R)\subset S$; then $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] and $\Omega_{A/R}$ is a finitely generated $A$-module. Choose generators $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_n$ of $\Omega_{A/R}$ and let $K\subset A^{\oplus n}$ be the kernel of $A^{\oplus n}\to\Omega_{A/R}$, $e_j\mapsto\omega_j$. The first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{A/R})\subset A$ is the ideal generated by all $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ minors of all $(n-1)\times n$ matrices whose rows are elements of $K$ (by convention $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{A/R})=A$ when $n\le1$); it does not depend on the choice of generators, and its formation commutes with localization $A\to A_g$ [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], so these ideals glue to a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega^1_{X/S})\subset\mathcal O_X$. The closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] of $X$ cut out by this ideal sheaf is denoted $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\hookrightarrow X$ and is called the first-Fitting singular subscheme of $f$.
